note: Outside the stated ICP on four of five criteria. He is a clergy member and chaplain running four to six part-time jobs including rideshare driving, not a business owner or physician; he is explicitly living paycheck to paycheck with a couple of hundred dollars a month spare and under half of $150,000 a year; and health is not the neglected area but the dominant one — type 1 diabetes, medicated hypertension, neuropathy and an abdominal wall separation under active physical therapy. This is rescue, not good-to-great: he is the heaviest he has ever been at 62 and wants to arrest the trend. He scrapes a match on the exclusion criterion only — he is not gym-averse, having held a membership for a year and done Taekwondo, and is chasing 20 to 40 pounds rather than 50. Worth recording that the rep reached the same conclusion live and said so — 'I don't know that it's going to be a perfect fit' — which is the correct outcome, but he arrived at it on affordability alone, never on the clinical picture.
